title: T1132.002 — Data Encoding - Non-Standard Encoding
subtitle: Watch a custom XOR channel from install to block, then read the same story as written steps.

nodes.label: Sensitive data
nodes.tip: Sensitive data - What is at risk

steps.title: chip:'Implant' - Implant checks in
steps.caption: The implant is installed on the victim PC and sends its first check-in to the C2 server. The 96-byte body is XOR encoded, so it looks like random noise.
steps.defender: the handshake bytes look random - no Base64 padding, no readable words.

steps.title: chip:'Key' - Key derived from the host ID
steps.caption: The implant builds its XOR key from the host ID. The key is computed on the host and never travels in clear text.
steps.defender: the key stays local, so stealing it needs the implant binary, not a network tap.

steps.title: chip:'XOR task' - C2 delivers an XOR task
steps.caption: The C2 server answers with a task encoded under the rolling XOR key. The implant decodes it and runs the command.
steps.defender: this is not Base64 - no padding, no recognizable alphabet, just raw binary.

steps.title: chip:'Custom reply' - Reply in a custom alphabet
steps.caption: The victim encodes the command output with a custom alphabet: digits 0 - 9 and letters a - y. Standard decoders do not know this character set.
steps.defender: the character set matches no standard scheme, and the letter z is simply absent.

steps.caption: An analytics rule compares character sets and message sizes with baselines. The charset matches no baseline, and sizes repeat every 30 seconds.
steps.defender: analytics beat signatures here - a 0/95 charset match plus periodic sizes is a strong lead.

steps.caption: The SOC blocks the C2 address at the firewall, isolates the PC, and ships a Suricata rule that matches the session shape. IOCs go to the ISAC.
steps.defender: the rule watches shape, not content, so it keeps working after key rotation.
